properties.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 4117002 and 4117001 (recorded 2019-02-07; mapped 2019-03-14; active), joined into one outline; cross-checked against Pier 70 Design for Development Figure 6.4.2 - Building Height Maximum (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. OVERLAP FIX 2026-09-14: a project-wide overlap audit found this block spatially overlapping Potrero Power Station Block 3/4 in real-world coordinates near the two sites' shared border -- a genuine disagreement between Pier 70's and Potrero's independent transforms, not a same-site priority call. Clipped back from Potrero's blocks, since Potrero's transform was independently validated against real building bearings (Sophie Maxwell/UCSF) earlier in this project, while this specific southern edge of Pier 70 has not been satellite-verified. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): a batch color-region check found this block's committed shape was roughly 55-85m too far south and somewhat too wide versus the diagram's actual fill. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) across the combined H1/H2 area, split at the real internal divider (the dashed sub-division line at pixel x~1701-1746, using its midpoint x~1723 as the H1/H2 boundary), and extracted a clean rectangular contour (OpenCV) for this block at pixel (1466,1300)-(1723,1462). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Re-confirmed zero overlap with Potrero Block 3/4 (the cross-site fix above still holds with this new, smaller shape) and zero overlap with H2. CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (street/curb re-anchoring pass, prompted by a user question about validation process consistency): this block's own north edge was directly confirmed, by rendering it against Esri World Imagery, to sit on top of real, currently-paved, actively-used street pavement (visible lane markings and/or vehicles in the satellite image), not a corner-lot sliver -- one of several Pier 70 blocks found this way after this project switched its real-street reference from OSM (community-traced, name-matched ways) to DataSF's own official Street Centerline / Curbs and Islands datasets (src/street_geometry.py), which for the first time gave an accurate enough curb position to see it. Clipped via shapely difference() against the corrected real-street buffer (6.8m centerline half-width, empirically measured against real curb data near Pier 70 -- see street_geometry.py); area 4025 -> 2536 sq m. The clip's result was a MultiPolygon (the street cut disconnected a 114 sq m sliver from the main body); kept only the larger piece, consistent with how this project has handled the same situation elsewhere (Mission Rock Square, Potrero Block 7). This is a targeted correction of this block's street-facing edge, not a re-verified re-trace of its other edges, which still carry this site's usual diagram-transform uncertainty. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the Assessor identifiers named in this log (Building 14's footprint as blklot 4052001; Building 12's Assessor parcel as blklot 4114010) come from DataSF (Building Footprints and Assessor parcels; repo copies in data/raw), not from the D4D cited for this file. Blklot 4052001 is a legacy lot: DataSF retired it on 2018-10-02 (Assessor parcels, acdm-wktn), its footprints carry mblr SF4052001, and the footprint layer does not name any of them 'Building 14'. Blklot 4114010 is an active lot at 1070 Maryland St that DataSF does not name 'Building 12'; that identity rests on the address given in tenant sources. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (Port Item 11A, Aug 2026: the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'), and no source read ties it to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor parcels include new lots created for the 28-acre district in 2019, without street addresses, but which lot (if any) is this block's was not established. It currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data -- see digitization_method.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat. Status planned: Port Item 11A (Aug 2026) says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward.'. REPLACED 2026-10-10 (shape; status and use unchanged): the owner asked for the planned blocks that have Assessor lots under them to use those lots. DataSF's Assessor layer (data/raw/parcels.geojson) has the union of Assessor lots 4117002 and 4117001 (4,723 m2, active, recorded 2019-02-07), 87% of our earlier trace lies inside it and the trace covers 47% of it; against the satellite imagery the lot lines sit on the real block edges where the trace was a few metres off. The outline is now their union using the lots' own vertices (no simplification), in place of the traced shape of 2,530 m2. The lots were assigned by the owner from the plan diagrams; they extend south of the block edge the D4D draws. geometry_type is now 'real' because the edges are recorded lot lines. The earlier sign-off covered the traced shape; this replacement was made at the owner's direction. 2026-10-11 CORRECTION to the 2026-10-10 entry above (text only; the shape is unchanged): its sentence 'against the satellite imagery the lot lines sit on the real block edges where the trace was a few metres off' was repeated across several Pier 70 shapes and does not describe this one. The lots are 4,723 m2 against a trace of 2,530 m2, and the trace covers only 47% of the lot union. No satellite comparison of this shape's edges is recorded, so the sentence is withdrawn for it. No change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type. Public text that said the lots were 'assigned by the owner' now says 'Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams'. 2026-10-12 accuracy audit (text only; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type): the superseded 2026-10-02 wording quoted above said the block 'currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building'. No source read gives this block's ground condition, so that statement is withdrawn; the current accuracy_caveat does not make it. What the D4D does support is only the passage between the two parcels: D4D S5.5.2 (PDF p.156, printed p.140), 'Loading spaces shall be permitted in mid-block passages on the following identified locations: ... Between parcels H1 and H2'. No Port or Assessor document read pairs lots 4117001, 4117002 and 4117003 with H1 or H2, which is why the accuracy_caveat calls the pairing Pier & Point's reading.
properties.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 4117002 and 4117001, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. The lots are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams: the parcel number is placed at the upper left of its parcel, and the H1 and H2 labels sit on either side of the dashed mid-block passage, so lots 4117002 and 4117001 are H1 and lot 4117003 is H2. No document read names these lots. The lots extend south of the block edge the D4D draws, into the former power-plant ground, so the outline is larger than the diagram's block. A building may sit back from the lot lines. No vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: No document names the Assessor lot of Parcel H1. Lots 4117002 and 4117001 (active) were assigned to it from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams, so its outline is their union.
properties.regulatory_context: Flexible commercial-office/residential parcel: D4D Figure 2.1.1 stripes H1 as Commercial-Office and Residential; the baseline (Mid-Point) and Maximum Residential scenarios show it residential and only the Maximum Office scenario shows it commercial. 90 ft max per Figure 6.4.2; six stories for commercial buildings and nine for residential (D4D Section 6.4.2). An earlier note citing Brookfield's leasing brochure (pure office use; a combined ~430,000 RSF for H1-H2) was removed 2026-09-29 because the brochure is not cited or retrieved. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Parcel H1 of the Pier 70 Design for Development, shown as the union of Assessor lots 4117002 and 4117001 (see the accuracy note). Status planned: Port Item 11A (Aug 2026) says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward.
